Since these are two separate events, I should use the principle of inclusion-exclusion here. That is, the probability of at least one palindrome occurring is equal to the probability of a letter palindrome plus the probability of a digit palindrome minus the probability of both happening at the same time. 

So, mathematically, that would be:

P(at least one palindrome) = P(letters palindrome) + P(digits palindrome) - P(letters palindrome AND digits palindrome)

First, let's compute the total number of possible license plates. Since there are three letters and each letter can be any of 26 letters (assuming the English alphabet), and three digits each being any of 10 digits (0-9), the total number of license plates is 26^3 * 10^3. Therefore, P(letters palindrome) = 1/26, P(digits palindrome) = 1/10.

Since the letters and digits are independent, the probability that both are palindromes is (1/26) * (1/10) = 1/260.
